title: PowerLens: An Adaptive DVFS Framework for Optimizing Energy Efficiency in Deep Neural Networks
problem: Current DVFS methods for DNNs rely on historical processor utilization and task computational load, leading to frequency ping-pong, response lag, and poor generalizability across different platforms and workloads.
motivation: DVFS can enhance energy efficiency in DNNs without modifying network architecture, addressing critical power management challenges in resource-constrained systems.
method: PowerLens identifies which parts of a neural network consume power similarly and groups them together to find optimal points for processor speed adjustment. For each group, it automatically selects the ideal processor frequency using an algorithm, without needing historical processor activity data. The method is then carefully trained and tested to work across different hardware platforms.
key_novelty: PowerLens automatically identifies where to optimize power by grouping neural network components that behave similarly in power consumption, rather than relying on historical processor activity data.
contributions: Power-sensitive feature extraction method for DNNs to characterize power behavior
Clustering-based identification of critical power blocks for adaptive DVFS instrumentation
Decision model for adaptive frequency preset per power block
Cross-platform adaptability framework for DVFS deployment on different hardware
